analysis.one_liner: Union Bank of India is a public-sector bank offering deposits, retail and corporate loans, and treasury services across India, majority owned by the Government of India.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (quarter ended September 2026), reported in October 2026, showed standalone net profit of ₹5,537 crore, up about 30% year-on-year, with net interest income up roughly 20%. Gross NPA fell to 2.42% and net NPA to 0.42%, continuing a multi-quarter clean-up. The board has separately approved an ₹8,000 crore capital raise (₹3,000 crore equity plus ₹5,000 crore bonds), the status of which (approved vs. executed) is not yet confirmed.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a government-owned bank that lends money and takes deposits, and it currently looks healthy on paper: profits are rising, bad loans are shrinking, and it holds more capital than regulators require. The tension is that the stock still sits well below where it traded in 2010, the bank is about to ask shareholders for fresh equity capital which could dilute existing holders, and its loan book is growing faster than its deposit base, which is a funding question worth watching rather than an immediate problem.
analysis.quarters: NIM has expanded for three straight quarters (2.70% in FY25-26 to 2.80% in Q1 FY27 to 2.86% in Q2 FY27), gross NPA has fallen from 2.65% (Q1 FY27) to 2.42% (Q2 FY27), and net profit growth has held near 30% YoY in both quarters. Management guided to credit growth broadly in line with the system (~18-19%), with actual growth running a bit ahead. These figures come from secondary news aggregators rather than the company's own filing or Screener, so treat the exact decimals as indicative pending direct verification.
analysis.performance_read: The stock closed at ₹183.16, still 37% below its October 2010 peak of ₹290.64 - and there have been no splits or demergers in this period (has_corporate_action is false), so this is a genuine 16-year failure to reclaim the old high, not a chart artifact. Against that, recent momentum has been strong: the stock is up 32% over 1 year versus Nifty's -12%, up 111% over 3 years versus Nifty's 18%, and up 345% over 5 years versus Nifty's 25% - all comfortably ahead of peer Canara Bank too. The honest read is a long, painful round trip from the 2010 high followed by a genuine multi-year recovery that has outpaced the market recently.
analysis.valuation_read: At roughly 6.3x earnings and about 1x book value, the stock looks statistically cheap against a broader banking-sector average P/E near 12x. Why it is cheap: it is a PSU bank with government ownership overhang, periodic capital-raise dilution risk (the pending ₹8,000 crore raise), and a legacy of weaker asset quality than private banks - peers like Bank of Baroda (~6.5x P/E, ~0.7x P/B) and Canara Bank (~5.3-5.9x P/E, ~0.9x P/B) trade at similar discounts. Whether it is cheap is a separate question: the discount has persisted across the sector for years and may reflect structurally lower ROE and dilution risk rather than mispricing.
analysis.growth_read: Growth looks both volume- and margin-led: advances grew about 18.5% YoY while NIM also expanded each of the last three quarters, so the bank is not simply relying on wider spreads on a flat book. The caveat is that deposits grew only about 6.9% YoY, well behind advances, pushing the credit-deposit ratio to around 84% - loan growth is currently outrunning the deposit base funding it.
analysis.health_read: Gross NPA at 2.42% and net NPA at 0.42%, with a provision coverage ratio of 95.2%, suggest asset quality has improved materially and bad loans are well provided for. Capital adequacy (CRAR 17.94%, CET-1 16.05%) is comfortably above regulatory minimums, and ROA of roughly 1.2% indicates profits are being generated efficiently rather than through leverage. The business risk (legacy NPAs) appears to be resolving; the live concern is funding mix (loan growth outpacing deposits) rather than solvency, and the planned equity raise suggests management itself sees a need for a bigger capital cushion.
analysis.ownership_read: The Government of India holds 74.76% as the promoter, unchanged across recent quarters, and - as expected for a government promoter - there is no pledging of these shares. FII holding has dipped slightly to around 8.6% from about 9.4%, while mutual fund holding has risen to roughly 4.7%. DII shareholding figures conflicted sharply across sources (0.55% vs. 11.98%) and could not be reconciled, so no number is reported for that line. No marquee individual investor was identified on the register in the sources checked.
strengths: Standalone net profit of ₹5,537 crore in Q2 FY27, up ~30% year-on-year
Gross NPA down to 2.42% and net NPA to 0.42%, with a 95.2% provision coverage ratio
Net interest margin has expanded for three consecutive quarters, from 2.70% to 2.86%
Capital adequacy ratio of 17.94% with CET-1 at 16.05%, well above regulatory minimums
watchpoints: Board-approved ₹8,000 crore capital raise (₹3,000 crore equity + ₹5,000 crore bonds) - equity dilution risk if the equity portion is executed; execution status not yet confirmed
Deposit growth (~6.9% YoY) is lagging advances growth (~18.5% YoY), pushing the credit-deposit ratio to around 84%
Stock remains 37% below its October 2010 peak after 16 years, despite no intervening splits or demergers to explain the gap
Shareholding data for DII holding conflicts across sources and could not be verified
analysis.one_thing: Whether the ₹3,000 crore equity portion of the approved capital raise is executed, and at what price - that determines whether the current earnings and ROE trajectory holds per-share or gets diluted.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly results, valuation and shareholding figures were sourced from secondary news aggregators (not the company's own filing or Screener directly), so treat precise decimals as indicative pending direct verification. DII shareholding percentage is unverified due to conflicting sources and is not reported. Next results date and the equity raise's execution status could not be confirmed.
